description.first: Fullstack Showcase was born as an experimentation environment to explore different technologies and approaches to backend development within a single ecosystem.
description.second: Instead of concentrating all functionality in a single application, I decided to split the system into independent services. Each has a defined responsibility and uses a different technology.
description.third: The goal is to explore how these solutions can be integrated, maintaining a clear separation of responsibilities and allowing each service to evolve independently.

0.title: Independent services
0.description: Each API manages a specific domain within the system.

1.title: Backend technologies
1.description: Each service uses a different language and framework.

2.title: Integrated ecosystem
2.description: All components are part of a single solution.

serviceArchitecture.description: Explore the components and connections of the system to understand their responsibilities and communication mechanisms.

frontend.description: Web application responsible for presenting the interface and consuming the functionalities exposed by backend services.

details.1: Each service maintains its own endpoints
details.2: Does not require an intermediary backend

catalog.description: Service responsible for managing the product catalog and inventory-related operations.

details.1: Is responsible for write operations on catalog schema
details.2: Exposes endpoints to query products and manage inventory

orders.description: Service in charge of managing orders and inventory movements, coordinating with Catalog API when it needs product information or operations.

details.1: Communicates with Catalog API via HTTP
details.2: Manages its own data in the orders schema

analytics.description: Service oriented to query information from different domains to generate reports and metrics.

details.0: Queries the catalog and orders schemas
details.2: Does not modify information managed by other services

database.title: Database
database.description: Shared PostgreSQL instance containing independent schemas for catalog and orders domains.

details.0: Catalog schema: owned by Catalog API
details.1: Orders schema: owned by Orders API
details.2: Independent users and permissions for each service

frontendCatalog.title: Frontend → Catalog API
frontendCatalog.description: The frontend directly consumes Catalog API endpoints to query the catalog and inventory-related functionalities.

details.0: Direct communication between frontend and API
details.1: Queries and operations via REST endpoints
details.2: Catalog API manages its own domain

frontendOrders.title: Frontend → Orders API
frontendOrders.description: The frontend uses Orders API to access functionalities related to order management.

details.2: Orders API maintains its own business logic

frontendAnalytics.title: Frontend → Analytics API
frontendAnalytics.description: The frontend consumes Analytics API to query available reports and metrics.

details.2: The API performs queries using read-only access

ordersCatalog.title: Orders API → Catalog API
ordersCatalog.description: Orders API communicates with Catalog API to query product information and request inventory-related operations. This way, it maintains domain independence without directly accessing Catalog tables.

details.2: Catalog API retains responsibility over its data
details.3: No direct write operations from Orders to catalog schema

catalogDatabase.title: Catalog API → PostgreSQL
catalogDatabase.description: Catalog API manages product and inventory information in the catalog schema of PostgreSQL.

details.0: Read and write access to catalog schema
details.2: Is the service responsible for modifying this data

ordersDatabase.title: Orders API → PostgreSQL
ordersDatabase.description: Orders API manages its orders and inventory movements within the orders schema, keeping its data separate from those belonging to the catalog.

details.0: Read and write access to orders schema
details.2: Does not directly modify catalog schema

analyticsDatabase.title: Analytics API → PostgreSQL
analyticsDatabase.description: Analytics API directly queries catalog and orders schemas to obtain information from different domains and build reports and metrics.

details.2: Does not modify Catalog or Orders data
details.3: Allows performing analytical queries on shared information

technicalDecisions.title: Technical decisions
technicalDecisions.description: Each decision responds to a need of the project, seeking a balance between simplicity, separation of responsibilities and technological exploration.

0.title: Technological diversity
0.description: Using different technologies to develop independent services and demonstrate the ability to work with different backend ecosystems.
0.result: Explore different tools and demonstrate their integration within a single solution.

1.title: Architecture according to needs
1.description: Apply different architectural approaches depending on the complexity and responsibilities of each service, avoiding adding unnecessary complexity.
1.result: Maintain clear separation of responsibilities without replicating patterns that don't add value to all services.

2.title: Shared database
2.description: Use a single PostgreSQL instance with independent schemas to keep infrastructure simple and preserve separation of responsibilities.

details.2: Read and write permissions according to each API's responsibility

2.result: Reduce infrastructure complexity without losing logical data isolation.

3.title: Direct access for analytics
3.description: Allow Analytics API to query PostgreSQL schemas directly instead of relying on HTTP endpoints from other services.

details.1: Queries across catalog and orders schemas
details.2: Without modifying information managed by other APIs

3.result: Simplify data retrieval and facilitate efficient queries for reports, considering possible growth in data volume.

4.title: Low-cost deployment
4.description: Select hosting services that keep the project published without monthly costs.

details.2: AWS S3 and CloudFront for the frontend

4.result: Keep the project available with low-cost infrastructure, considering limitations of free plans such as suspension due to inactivity.
